title: pharn-ci Report v2
description: Machine-readable output of pharn-ci since 0.2.0. This schema is the source of truth: markdown and CLI text are renderings of this object. v2 is Report v1 (schema/report.v1.json) plus optional top-level objects: every v1 field keeps its name, type and meaning, and schemaVersion is the number 2. A missing optional object means that part did not run. Within schemaVersion 2 fields are never removed or retyped; new optional fields may only be added by updating this file. Format keywords are annotations.

message.description: A v1 message (schema/report.v1.json#/$defs/message) with the same fields and constraints. v2 documents its own codes here so codes added in v2 are listed in v2.

code.description: Stable identifier; branch on this, never on text. Known codes: DIFF_COVERAGE_BELOW_THRESHOLD, DIFF_COVERAGE_UNGATED, NO_COVERABLE_CHANGES, COVERAGE_FILE_MISSING, COVERAGE_FILE_EMPTY, COVERAGE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED, DIFF_UNAVAILABLE, NO_AGENT_SETUP_FILES. Every v1 code keeps its meaning and level in v2 (schema/report.v1.json documents COVERAGE_PATHS_UNMATCHED, COVERAGE_PATHS_PARTIALLY_UNMATCHED, CONFIG_CHANGED_IN_DIFF, COVERAGE_FILE_TRACKED, DIFF_BINARY_COVERED_FILE, AGENT_SETUP_FILE_EMPTY, TEST_FILES_DELETED, AGENT_SETUP_EXPECTED_MISSING and COVERAGE_LINES_SKIPPED). Codes added in v2: TEST_INTEGRITY_MODE_IGNORED (warn: .pharn/ci.yml set test_integrity.mode looser than the workflow input or the default, so it was ignored), TEST_INTEGRITY_OFF (info: the effective test-integrity mode is off), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI01 (TI01, test file deleted: error when a deleted or renamed-away test file defined tests and the mode is block, warn in mode warn, info when the change also deletes the source of the same name or its package, or adds a test file of the same name; every file is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI11 (TI11, CI stopped running tests: error when a workflow loses a test step or its pull request trigger and the mode is block, warn otherwise, including for a reduced matrix, an added continue-on-error, a disabling if: or a near-zero timeout; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals) and TEST_INTEGRITY_TI14 (TI14, diff-coverage exclusions widened: error when the check config lowers the coverage threshold or adds an exclusion and the mode is block, warn in mode warn; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI03 (TI03, a skip added to a test file: error when an unconditional skip is added to a test the diff shows existed and the mode is block, warn in mode warn; warn for a conditional skip, a skip inside a test body and a skip in a test the change adds; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals) and TEST_INTEGRITY_TI04 (TI04, a focused-run marker added to a JS/TS test file: error when .only, fit or fdescribe is added and the mode is block, warn in mode warn; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI10 (TI10, a test script in package.json weakened: error when an added test script ignores the exit status of a command, prints or exits 0 in place of running the tests, passes with no tests, or limits the run to a path or name pattern, or when a pretest or posttest script is removed, and the mode is block, warn in mode warn; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals) and TEST_INTEGRITY_TI13 (TI13, a coverage-ignore comment added to source: error when an Istanbul, V8 or C8 ignore hint or a coverage.py no-cover pragma is added to a JavaScript, TypeScript or Python file that is not a test file and the mode is block, warn in mode warn; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI08 (TI08, snapshot churn: warn when more than 10 snapshot files are changed in one change, when a JS/TS test file rewrites 10 or more inline snapshots, or when a snapshot-update flag is added to a test script in package.json or to a pytest config file; it never blocks, so the level is warn in modes block and warn; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI15 (TI15, the test may be special-cased: info when an added condition in a JavaScript, TypeScript or Python source file compares with a string or number literal that a test file in the same change also adds; it never blocks or warns, so the level is info in modes block and warn; at most 10 findings per change are in testIntegrity.signals and the text says how many more there are in each file) and TEST_INTEGRITY_TI16 (TI16, a lint or type suppression comment added to a JS/TS or Python test file: info in modes block and warn, so it never blocks and a report with only these findings passes; every finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TEXT_TRUNCATED (warn: the diff text of a file a test-integrity signal reads was cut at 5000 changed lines, so a finding past the cut is not seen; the message names those files and is not given in mode off), TEST_INTEGRITY_ACCEPTED (info, Action only: a reviewer who is not the PR author applied the accept label, so every block signal was downgraded to warn; testIntegrity.accepted names the label and the reviewer) and TEST_INTEGRITY_ACCEPT_IGNORED (warn, Action only: the accept label was looked at and does not count, because the PR author applied it, a non-user account applied it, no labeling event was found, or the pull request or its events could not be read; the block signals stand), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI02 (TI02, a test removed: error when a test of a file that stays has no test of the same name or a similar body left in the touched test files and the mode is block, warn in mode warn and for a test whose name is computed; the signal sits at the base path and base line; the text names every file of the id and says how many findings the 20-per-file cap left out; every listed finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI05 (TI05, assertions emptied or dropped: error when a test that had assertions at base has none at head and calls no assertion helper and the mode is block, warn in mode warn, when a helper call may hold the assertions and when only some assertions are gone with the rest of the body unchanged; the text names every file of the id and the cap's count; every listed finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI06 (TI06, a test weakened: warn when a test that stays has a strong matcher replaced by a weak one, an assertion guard lowered or removed, an assertion that compares a literal with itself added, or an assertion moved into a try block that has a catch or after an early return; always warn in every mode; the signal sits at the head path and head line; the text names every file of the id and the cap's count; every listed finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI07 (TI07, expected value edited to match: warn in modes block and warn when a test of a modified JS/TS or Python test file changes only literals in the expected-value arguments of its assertions and the change also edits a source file; it never blocks; the text names every file of the id and the cap's count; every listed finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI09 (TI09, test config loosened: error when a test-runner setting that makes fewer tests run, lets a weaker run pass or lowers the coverage gate is changed in a touched config file (a lowered or removed coverage threshold, a narrowed test list, a widened exclusion, passWithNoTests, allowOnly or bail turned on, a grep added, forbidOnly turned off, a pytest addopts that gains a deselecting option) and the mode is block, warn in mode warn; always warn for a raised retry count or timeout and for a value that is not a literal and cannot be compared; the text names every file of the id and the cap's count; every listed finding is in testIntegrity.signals), TEST_INTEGRITY_TI12 (TI12, a module under test mocked: warn when a test file newly mocks a source file the change also adds, modifies or renames; always warn in every mode; one finding per test file and target; the text names every file of the id and the cap's count; every listed finding is in testIntegrity.signals) and TEST_INTEGRITY_INDEX_UNAVAILABLE (warn: touched JS/TS or Python test files could not be compared at the merge base and at HEAD, so TI02 and TI05 did not check them, or TI02 and TI05 did not run because the test text could not be read; touched test-config files could not be read, so TI09 did not check them, or TI09 did not run because the text of the config files could not be read; the message names the files with a reason code each, or the reason; it is not given in mode off). New codes may be added within v2; consumers must tolerate unknown codes. No code is removed or renamed before 1.0. Codes added in v0.4.0: the secret scan of the committed agent config files; a message names the shape id and up to 5 path and line locations, never the value or the key. AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S01 (error: a GitHub token), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S02 (error: an Anthropic API key), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S03 (error: an OpenAI API key), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S04 (error: a Google API key), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S05 (error: an AWS access key ID), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S06 (error: a Slack token), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S07 (error: a Stripe live key), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S08 (error: a private key), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S09 (error: a password or token in a URL), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S10 (warn: a secret-like value under a secret-named key), AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_S11 (info: a literal value under a secret-named key in a file that loads its other secrets from the environment) and AGENT_CONFIG_SECRET_UNSCANNED (error when a file was dropped as too-large, over-file-cap, over-total-cap or unsafe-path, otherwise warn: the agent config files were not scanned, or only some of them were). POLICY_UNAVAILABLE (warn, or error when the workflow sets policy: required: the org policy could not be fetched or used, so the check ran with the workflow inputs and .pharn/ci.yml; the message names a reason, the HTTP status when there is one and the request id the app sent) and POLICY_OVERRIDE_IGNORED (warn: a setting looser than the org policy, or one a policy file may not set, was not applied; the message names each setting and the layer it came from, at most 20, and no value except the two numbers of a coverage threshold). UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE (warn: the run was not uploaded because the report is larger than the upload limit; the check ran in full). POLICY_P08 (error, or the level the org policy sets for P08: tracked files match a forbidden file pattern of the org policy; the message names up to 20 paths and the count) and POLICY_P09 (error, or warn for an agent settings file whose direction is not judged yet: the change edits a file the org policy guards; the message names up to 20 paths and the count; each reason is in policy.violations). POLICY_P11 (error, or warn when the org policy sets agents.protected_paths_mode or the rule to warn: an agent pull request changes paths the org policy protects, or could not be checked because the diff, or the policy file at the merge base, could not be read; the message names up to 20 paths and the evidence as fixed words, never a pattern, label or login) and AGENT_PR_DETECTION_INCOMPLETE (warn: the pull request counts as an agent PR because its evidence could not be read in full, and the org policy protects paths; the message names the reason as one fixed word). POLICY_P02, POLICY_P03, POLICY_P04, POLICY_P05 and POLICY_P06 (error, or warn for the additionalDirectories check of P02, or the level the org policy sets for the rule: the committed agent settings or MCP files break org policy rule P02, P03, P04, P05 or P06; the message names up to 20 locations as path and line, and the count; each reason is in policy.violations) and POLICY_SETTINGS_INVALID (warn, or error for a file pharn-ci could not read or a problem a required list depends on: the rules P02 to P06 could not fully use an agent settings or MCP file, or did not run; the message names up to 20 problems as path, line and reason, never file text). POLICY_P07 (warn by default, error when the org policy sets setup.consistency or the rule to block, info when it sets info or the agent instruction files could not be read: agent instruction files in the same directory name different package managers or JavaScript test runners, or some of them could not be compared; the message names up to 20 files, and each violation a path, a line and the tools as fixed words, never the file's text).

testIntegrity.description: Test-integrity findings for the change under review. mode: the effective mode (block | warn | off); source: where it came from; verdict: from the signals and the mode; languages: which detectors ran; accepted: set by the Action when a reviewer who is not the PR author applied the accept label to a pull request run in mode block; acceptLabel: the Action's accept-label input when it is not the default.

acceptLabel.description: The name of the accept label the Action was given in its accept-label input. Written by the Action only, and only when it is not the default pharn/accepted (compared case-insensitively); absent from a CLI report and from a default run. At most 50 characters.

accepted.description: Who signed off the block findings. Written by the Action only: label is the accept label as configured, by is the login of the user account (not the PR author) that applied it. Null or absent when nothing was accepted.

languages.description: Which syntax-aware detectors ran: ts, js, py, go. Empty in 0.2.x, whose signals read diff lines only; from 0.3.0 the test indexes fill ts, js and py with the sorted languages of the test files they parsed at the merge base or at HEAD (the Go detectors are not shipped).

changes.description: The tests-changed summary: the tests the touched JS/TS and Python test files add, remove, modify or rename between the merge base and HEAD. Present only when at least one test changed; absent when no touched test file was compared, when the mode is off, and when the comparison did not run. added: a test new at head that matches no base test; removed: a base test that nothing at head stands for, at its base path and base line; modified: a test of the same full name in the same file whose body or modifiers differ; renamed: a test matched to a test of another name or in another file. Every entry except a removed one sits at its head path and head line. The four lists hold at most 200 entries in all, filled in the order removed, modified, renamed, added, each sorted by path and line; totals and files count every test.

totals.description: How many tests changed, by kind. Counts every test, including those the 200-entry cap left out of the lists.

added.description: Tests new at head that match no base test.

removed.description: Base tests that nothing at head stands for.

modified.description: Tests of the same full name in the same file whose body or modifiers differ.

renamed.description: Tests matched to a test of another name or in another file.

files.description: One row per test file that has at least one changed test, sorted by path. Counts every test of the file, including those the 200-entry cap left out of the lists.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the test file (its base path for a removed test).

language.description: The language of the test file by its extension.

renamed.description: Tests of this file renamed or moved to it.

added.description: The tests added, sorted by path then line, at their head path and head line. Subject to the 200-entry cap across the four lists.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the test file: the head path, or the base path for a removed test.

name.description: The full name of the test, the names of its enclosing blocks and its own joined with ' › '. Control characters are turned into spaces, and a name longer than 120 UTF-16 code units is cut to 120, ending with an ellipsis, never inside a surrogate pair.

line.description: The line of the test in its file: the head line, or the base line for a removed test.

removed.description: The tests removed, sorted by path then line, at their base path and base line. Subject to the 200-entry cap across the four lists; filled first.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the test file: the head path, or the base path for a removed test.

name.description: The full name of the test, the names of its enclosing blocks and its own joined with ' › '. Control characters are turned into spaces, and a name longer than 120 UTF-16 code units is cut to 120, ending with an ellipsis, never inside a surrogate pair.

line.description: The line of the test in its file: the head line, or the base line for a removed test.

modified.description: The tests modified, sorted by path then line, at their head path and head line. Subject to the 200-entry cap across the four lists; filled second.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the test file: the head path, or the base path for a removed test.

name.description: The full name of the test, the names of its enclosing blocks and its own joined with ' › '. Control characters are turned into spaces, and a name longer than 120 UTF-16 code units is cut to 120, ending with an ellipsis, never inside a surrogate pair.

line.description: The line of the test in its file: the head line, or the base line for a removed test.

renamed.description: The tests renamed or moved, sorted by path then line, at their head path and head line. Subject to the 200-entry cap across the four lists; filled third.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the test file: the head path, or the base path for a removed test.

name.description: The full name of the test, the names of its enclosing blocks and its own joined with ' › '. Control characters are turned into spaces, and a name longer than 120 UTF-16 code units is cut to 120, ending with an ellipsis, never inside a surrogate pair.

line.description: The line of the test in its file: the head line, or the base line for a removed test.

truncated.description: How many tests the 200-entry cap left out of the four lists. Absent when none were left out.

meta.description: Run metadata, present when the Action ran. Absent from a CLI run.

isAgentPr.description: true when the pull request counts as an agent PR, including when detection could not read all of its evidence; false when the run has no pull request.
